caveats: One v1.0.5 control and two sequential runs of the same merged-main binary on a shared, busy development host; not performance percentiles or an availability SLA.
Synthetic signed repository: six suites, two hostnames served by one loopback origin, 5000 filler rows per index, 48 real packages, 12 index variants per suite with six unique blobs.

150 ms index delay and 30 s package delay apply only to the measured generation. Package delays are removed before the final installation, so this measures candidate visibility, not installation latency under a continuing outage.
The same client polls with apt-get update every five seconds after each update finishes; updates themselves may wait. The fixture uses canonical indexes, without Acquire-By-Hash.
Refresh and warming budget are omitted from configuration: each binary uses its own defaults. Cooldown is 60 seconds and max concurrent adoptions is two for both.
Client requests can trigger checks; this is not a measurement of the periodic scheduler in isolation.
Main has a canonical-index publication barrier that v1.0.5 lacks. The comparison measures the complete versions, not just one change.
Daemon event timestamps are taken by the harness when logs arrive. Per-suite client visibility is the first completed APT observation with all eight relevant packages at version 2.0.
